counterfactual_missing_items: No evidence of infiltrative growth or recurrence typical of lipofibromatosis
Lesion stable for years from infancy, favoring a congenital hamartoma over a neoplasm
decisive_items: a skin-colored, exophytic, soft, oval tumor with overlying pinpoint vessels and branching telangiectasia
The lesions are composed of mature adipose and fibrous tissues
soft tissue mass on her right flank
response.rationale: R2 matches the classic clinical and histological features of nevus lipomatosus superficialis: stable congenital exophytic soft tumor with telangiectasia and mature adipose-fibrous tissue. R3 relies only on histology and lacks clinical specificity. C1 is only an anatomic refinement of R2 with no raw support.

rejected.why: No raw support spans; only an append-only anatomic completion of R2, not independently evidenced.
Histology alone is nonspecific; clinical stability since infancy and exophytic telangiectatic appearance favor nevus lipomatosus superficialis over lipofibromatosis.
